newsitem.title: CHINA: HK stocks open sharply up on Wall Street rebound.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks open sharply up on Wall Street rebound.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks opened sharply higher on Tuesday with the blue chip Hang Seng Index up 150 points, or 0.91 percent, to 16,611 in early trade, following a rebound on Wall Street.
"Sentiment improved since Wall Street is likely to find good support at the 8,000 level and the U.S. long bond yield is seen steadier," said Charles Cheung, executive director at J&A Securities.
The Dow industrials rose 30.89 points to close on Monday at 8,062.11 after it tumbled 156.78 points to 8,031.22 last Friday.

Active buying was seen on banks and red-chips which boosted the Hang Seng to an early high of 16,660.76, up 200.29 points, before it retreated to 16,487, up 26 points in the first half hour of Tuesday's trading. Turnover was HK$4.35 billion.

"The market was a bit overexcited by the rebound on Wall Street and a retreat on Hang Seng is normal since banks have increased mortgage rates and this will affect local property prices," said Antony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas.
Higher mortgage rates could dampen home buyers' interest, Mak said. HSBC and Standard Chartered Bank recently raised mortgage rates 25 basis points to 9.25 percent.
Shares of HSBC added HK$3.00 to HK$273.00 and its unit Hang Seng Bank shares rose HK$0.50 to HK$109.00.
Cheung Kong eased HK$0.25 to HK$93.50 and Sun Hung Kai Properties fell HK$1.00 to HK$101.00.
The Hang Seng Chinese Enterprises Index surged 58.03 points, or 4.27 percent, to 1,415.71.
"Mainland Chinese money and small local investors are seen actively buying H-shares and red-chips," said Michael Ng, dealing director at Sassoon Securities.
Petrochemical stocks led the rise on hopes possible corporate restructurings could lead to asset injections.
Tianjin Bohai topped the gainers, jumping HK$0.50, or 22.22 percent, to HK$2.75. Yizheng surged HK$$0.30 to HK$4.625 and Jilin Chemical added HK$0.20 to HK$2.225.
